utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Am I correct, Mr. Black, that you had finished your leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, although I haven't spoken with the witness I notice he has a chart and it may be in response to the Chamber's question. Perhaps it would be appropriate to deal with that before he starts his cross-examination. But I leave it in Your Honour's hands since it was a Bench's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you have any further things to put on the -- in evidence? Is this the document you want to put it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two things. First of all there is the chart you requested the first session which I sent to the Prosecution an electronic version because I think it would be better if it would be printed in colour so to make it more easy for you to see the various functions. And then secondly, I understood that I didn't really manage to explain the Posavina corridor to you on Friday so I looked in my -- in documents I have at home this weekend and I found a map prepared by UNPROFOR - I think it was in 1994 or 1995 - that depicts the corridor in a much clearer way than I tried to explain on Friday. And if you want, Your Honours, I can explain the legend and so on on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Have you shown a copy of this map to -- has it been shown to the Defence? Mr. Black?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have not seen it myself. I don't believe it's been shown to the Defence, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you haven't seen this document, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have a problem. The Accused is not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. Can that be attended to before we proceed? Okay. With the help of the usher, may this be given to Mr. Black so that you can lead your witness about that document, and the bar chart that the Court asked for, please, if you may. Otherwise the Court will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, good morning.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you have another copy of this with you or is the only copy, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the only copy I brought, Your Honours. I apologise for the confusion but I gave a copy to the legal officer and asked for the best way to proceed and I see now that we are going to put it in evidence. But if you want I can explain on the ELMO, if that is feasible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would propose that we do just that. I'll make sure if it's been sent to us that at the next break we have colour copies to distribute to the Court and to the Defence. If you want we can go ahead and he can explain it and maybe we can put this one in evidence and give copies later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. With the assistance of the usher I'll hand this back to the witness and if you could please place it on the ELMO. And, Your Honours, I believe the best way to see this on the ELMO is to press the video evidence button on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, looking to your right there at the map on the ELMO, could you please explain what's shown here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this map shows a section of northwestern Bosnia-Herzegovina, which during the conflict became known as the Posavina corridor. The map, and maybe you cannot see the legend but it's more to the bottom, the map was prepared by the mapping survey of the United Kingdom Ministry of Defence in 1995. It's indicated on the right bottom corner, who provided also maps to UNPROFOR. On the map, the electronic map, the times map on Friday I drew a line which more or less went from Bijeljina, Brcko and then further to the west. Well, this was exactly the location of the Posavina corridor. The red lines are the confrontation lines between the warring factions whereby the area here, the so-called Orasje pocket, that was on the Bosnian Croat, also known as HVO control in the conflict, and then the territory south of this red line was in the control of the ABiH, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or Bosniak controlled armed forces, and the corridor went in between these lines, from the east Serbia to the west, Bosanska Krajina, so the western part of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well as the territory or the entity known as the SAO Krajina and subsequently the RSK. Just for your information, the blue line is an UNPA border and this is the UNPA east so sector east, which -- I mean, the southern part of sector east which consisted of what we can't see on the map but in the northern part, Baranja, and inside of that, eastern Slavonia and western Srem. So I just brought this map to you, Your Honours, now to be more accurate in describing the Posavina corridor to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this receive a number and be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document will then be admitted into evidence and may it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may deal with the bar chart, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And, again, I apologise for the confusion about the copies. Does the Court have or does the Registry have a copy of the bar chart? I don't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, perhaps, do you have it with you or what's the status of the bar chart?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The status, Your Honour, is that the chart is finished what I prepared in colour and I don't have a colour printer so I understood from Friday's session that I was allowed to send it to the Prosecution. So I sent it this morning to the Prosecution and I assumed that they are in a possibility to prepare colour copies which would make it easier to explain it to you. I don't have a copy of it with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is it possible that maybe during your cross-examination or maybe during your re-examination, you might hand this in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution now has a colour copy. So whenever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could -- as soon -- as soon as we have those printed I can signal that to the Court. I'll stand up and mention it and then we can deal with it either during cross examination or, if you prefer, we can wait until redirect. However is easiest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. When the copies are ready we'll get the message from the parties. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic? The witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens. I'm Predrag Milovancevic, attorney-at-law, counsel for Mr. Martic, and on behalf of the Defence team I will be cross-examining you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As the situation requires, we shall begin from the very beginning, from your CV, and we will cover it very briefly. I'm interested in only several brief issues. You stated, Mr. Theunens, that you graduated from a military academy in Belgium; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The military academy that you completed, is that the main military school where officers of the Belgian army are schooled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And I could be more complete. It's actually the only school where or the only academy where officers are trained or at least as you would call it, professional officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand my previous question? What I had in mind was comparison with the education system in the former Yugoslavia, where in addition to the military academy, there were also staff schools. For example, various kinds of expertise could be acquired at these staff schools. Did they not exist in Belgium in addition to the military academy?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I think I misunderstood the question, then, but at least in Belgium and at the time when I became an officer it was rather difficult to be admitted to one of the, let's say, post-military academy officer trainings. It existed. There was for example, there is a school which we call the -- it's now called the Defence College but at the time it was called the Royal Higher Military Institute. Some people call it even war school. And there basically three staff courses were given, the first one what was something we called the short -- excuse me, the first cycle, which was I think at the time when I attended it a three weeks' or four weeks' course which was intended for lieutenants, lieutenants to captains, to learn how to work in a battalion staff. The second one I attended and the second one is mentioned in my CV under the heading 3, summary of professional skills. The second one was what we called among the military the second cycle, which is a one year course or one school year, which is a senior officer candidate course so where people who of the rank of captain or commandant, which is a Belgian rank between captain and major, learn how to work in a brigade staff and people from the army, of course, learn how to work in an army brigade staff, people from the navy they learn -- the navy doesn't have brigades but they learn how to work in a staff at a similar level in the navy and the same for the air force. After that, there is also what I would call the third cycle, which is the senior staff course, which -- where people obtain -- where people who are specially selected obtain what we call a staff degree or a staff diploma. In French it would be Brevet d'Etat Major which is intended for people with the rank of major or sometimes lieutenant colonel and there they learn how to work in a corps or even a higher level staff. But again there is no way how -- you cannot attend the third cycle without having attended military academy and the same applies now also for the second cycle, even though at the time when I joined the Belgian military, there were also people who entered the military directly without having -- excuse me, they entered the military directly and obtained an officer degree without having attended the four or five year cycle at military academy which I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In order to enroll into the third cycle, as you call it, in addition to completing an undergraduate degree, did one also need a certain experience, a certain number of years in service in the military?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not so sure about the undergraduate degree. I didn't translate the title I obtained in military academy into an English degree or into a bachelor or a master because, and maybe you're aware of that, in the European Union, I think it's the Bologna Decree, there are efforts made to find or to standardise, I would say, university degrees between in a bachelor level would generally be three years and a master's level which would be four to five years. [French spoken] in French is a four-year study plus then six months in armour school and I haven't been able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Theunens. I apologise for interrupting you. My question was aimed at something else. I don't want to waste everybody's time here. In order to enroll into a third cycle course, did one need a certain experience, a certain number of years spent working as an officer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I saw the expression "undergraduate degree" I think it was helpful to explain that to the court because it applies directly to my experience. Now to answer the second part of the question, years of experience applies to any course in the military. You could not, for example, attend the second cycle I attended without having at least ten years experience as an officer. Of course, it applies to the third cycle, but there, because it's only a limited number of officers that attend, there is also a whole selection process. So in fact people, officers who have finished the second cycle, after one or two years, they can apply for the third cycle and then they have to undergo a selection process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, now, in addition to the military academy, which is a pre-requirement for an education of an officer, what other levels have you completed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I explained, I finished the second cycle and this is visible, if I could call it like the second cycle, it is visible under the heading 3 of my CV under the title summary of professional skills. And there it reads from September 1997 until July 1998 I attended the staff course or senior officer candidate course at the Royal Superior Defence Institute in Brussels.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I think that it was important to expand on the information provided in the CV, which is not very extensive. My next question pertains to a fact stated in your work experience, where you say that you were commander in a tank unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, from May 1998 [sic] until May 1990 when I served in the second guides regiment with the Belgian armed forces in Germany I was a platoon commander and particularly during the second year I also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you say from May 1998 to May 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, May 1988 until May 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I served as a platoon commander in the second guides regiment in -- with the Belgian armed forces in Germany. During the second year because my company commander was following courses, a second language for French courses, to attend staff course, I had to replace him at several occasions and also I -- doing a certain time period I accomplished or carried out the tasks of a second commander of a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is a tank platoon a basic armoured unit within the Belgian army? Is that a basic and lowest tactical unit as it is, for examples in various NATO countries?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, you could describe it like that but actually when you look at the ways how tank units are used, the company is actually the smallest unit. We would rarely operate as a separate platoon because that wouldn't make much sense from the armoured warfare point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Armoured units in which you served as an officer, were they three partite or four partite? I'm asking you this because as far as I was able to see it seems that the Warsaw Pact had four partite units composed out of four elements and NATO countries usually had units composed out of three elements.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure whether I understand the question correctly but a tank platoon, as it was in the regiment where I was serving would consist of four tanks. A company would consist of three platoons. That would mean 12 tanks plus then one tank for the company commander and we would actually call the company a squadron, and a tank Battalion would then be -- would consist of three armoured companies, i.e., 39 tanks and one tank for the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let me just see if I understood you well. A tank platoon has four tanks and a tank company has three platoons, so therefore it's a three partite makeup. That's what I wanted to know, three times four means 12 tanks plus a command tank. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The fact that from May 1988 to May 1990, you served as commander of a tank platoon for one year and then after that, occasionally acted as a commander of a tank company, did I interpret this right? Does this fact mean that for one year, you were a commander of a unit which was composed of four tanks and that occasionally, you acted as a commander of a unit which has 12 or 13 armoured vehicles?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's not entirely correct because there was no clear division. In a sense that when I mentioned in my CV it was acting commander of a tank company I remained platoon commander for two years and, because I was the most senior platoon commander in that company, when the company commander was not available, I was to replace him. And that's common to any military procedure that when the commander isn't there, then his deputy or an acting commander will replace him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I apologise if I misunderstood anything you said previously. Now we have clarified this. Can you please tell us, until what year did you serve as an active officer in command of a military unit, be it either a platoon or a company, a tank one in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as is mentioned in my CV, in May 1990, the battalion commander asked me whether I wanted to become his personnel officer, so S1. And, okay, then I ceased to be a platoon commander and also acting company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that following that, for one year, you were a commander of the first year cadets at the polytechnics division?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, after having been a personnel officer on S1 in the second guides regiment I was called to return to the military academy. The position to which I was assigned was a deputy commander of a promotion, as we call it, so deputy commander of first years because there was also a commander. However, I think it was in December or January of that year, the commander decided to leave. He left the military. And then I was appointed to replace him, so I stayed commander there of the first -- that part of the first years until July or -- yeah, until July or August. I think that was 1991, if I recall well. Excuse me, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you tell us when did you stop serving in the units of the Belgian armed forces, serving as an officer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this moment I'm still an officer in the Belgian armed forces even though since the 28th of June 2001 when I started to work here, I was seconded to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is the short answer that you were an active member until 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I don't think that would be correct, Your Honours, because even though I'm not serving at the moment theoretically I could always be called back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you're not active.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not active but I'm not a reservist either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question was were you actively involved up until 2001.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours. That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if we understood each other well. What I had in mind was something stated in your CV, namely that in September of 1992, you became an analyst for the Balkans, and you remained in that post until June of 1999. This was a post within the Belgian General Staff.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was not a post within the Belgian General Staff but a post within the Belgian military intelligence and security service which at that time responded directly to the Minister of Defence. There has been a restructuring since I left, and now this -- the head of the service is also an assistant Chief of Staff who responds to the chief of defence military as well as the Minister of Defence. But all these organisations, all the bodies I mentioned, are part of the armed forces, Belgian armed forces, so as long as I stayed there I was still a member of the Belgian armed forces. I would like to add that even though it was not a combat unit but when I served in Sarajevo, from December 1998 until May 1999, I was in charge of what is called a national intelligence cell. I also had to command people even though not for combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Is it correct, then, that in September of 1992 you stopped working as a command officer in the sense of combat use of units and command of units, and that you moved into the area of military intelligence and worked there as an officer once again, which is a fact that we do not challenge?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formulated this way, Your Honours, I mean the answer would be yes or the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. We have now completed the part of the cross-examination which deals with your CV, your work experience and so on, and we will now turn to your expert report in this case. In describing the purpose of this report, on page 2 of your analysis, Mr. Theunens, do you state that the purpose of this report is to analyse the role of the SAO Krajina Territorial Defence and the RSK Territorial Defence as well as the role of the Serbian army of Krajina during the conflict in Croatia from 1991 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. That's one of the two purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this first aim, if we can call it so, was it your task to also analyse the links between Milan Martic and these organisations that we have just mentioned in the course of this conflict?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours but I saw, I mean I considered the links between Milan Martic and these organisations as the second purpose of the report or the second aim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Milovancevic, doesn't it say so expressly in his report, very first paragraph, the aim of there study is to analyse the role of the SAO Krajina, RSK TO and SVK during the conflict in Croatia from 1991 to 1995, and the relations between Milan Martic and these organisations throughout this conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will be more specific in putting my questions. It was unintentionally -- it was unintentional, the fact that this question was split into two parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would be very helpful if you could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In order to attain the purpose or aim of this study, did you divide this report into four parts, in such a way that parts 1 and 2 are necessary in order to understand parts 3 and 4? You then go on to say that it was not your intention to list in section 3 and 4 in detail the operations of the armed forces in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. Actually, I mentioned in this introduction that this analysis was not intended as a detailed account of all armed forces operations and more specifically I didn't analyse the role of organisations known as ZNG, HV, and maybe other armed forces that may have been involved in the conflict in Croatia between 1991 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, is it possible, Mr. Theunens, to study and analyse the role of one side in an armed conflict without simultaneously studying and analysing the acts of the other side, its deployment, its goals and tasks in specific missions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that is very well possible because this is a report on a certain topic and the topic has been explained. The role of the SAO Krajina, RSK TO, and SVK so to study that role and analyse it and second aspect the linkage or the relations between Milan Martic and these organisations. When you look around in libraries or on the internet you will find plenty of studies both conflict analysis which will, of course, look at the different parties but also studies on one specific party. It's not a conflict analysis. It is focused on two specific topics and even though at certain moments certain activities of the other side, if I could call it like that, are mentioned, I don't think that they were necessary -- I mean, I don't think a detailed study of the Croatian positions, armed forces, intentions and other aspects are necessary to understand how the SAO Krajina and RSK TO were established, how they functioned, who supported them and what the role of Milan Martic was between -- in organising, setting up and assisting these organisations, and, more importantly, in commanding and controlling these organisations where I would also like to add the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I fully understood the aim of this report, and it is precisely as you have just described it, Mr. Theunens, but my question was directed at something else, Mr. Theunens. Is it possible to study the role of the SAO Krajina Territorial Defence, the role of the TO of the Serbian Republic of Krajina and its army during the conflict in Croatia without previously establishing any cause and effect related issues, without establishing the role and the influence of the acts of the other side in this conflict?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wasn't that question answered? His question to -- the time you asked it the first time he said Your Honours I think that is very well possible because this is a report on a certain topic and the topic has been explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In order to attain the goal that you were facing, you have, as you have explained to us, split this material into four sections, and there is also an introductory part. You devoted your first chapter to the armed forces of the SFRY or rather that was section 1. Section 2 were the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia. Section 3 is Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina and RSK in 1991 to 1995. And section 4 is the SVK from May -- October 1992 to August 1995. Is this correct, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. I'm just checking the time period that applies to the -- to section 3 because I thought that it went from 1991 to 1992. And indeed, so I would like to make one small correction. Section 3 covers the time period 1991 to 1992 because, as explained in the report, in May 1992 and subsequently in October-November 1992, measures were taken at the level of the RSK or the entity known as the RSK, to transform the Territorial Defence into the SVK, the armed forces of the entity known as Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In section 2 of your analysis, which is entitled, "Armed forces of the Republic of Serbia," you give a summary of the contents therein, which is page 3 of your report, under item 2, armed forces of the Republic of Serbia. Under item 3, duties of the president, Minister of Defence, and Minister of the Interior in the Republic of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, and this is discussed on page 60 in the English version of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 57 in the English version, Mr. Theunens, in the summary under item 1A, you say that this section describes the legislative framework that applied to defence matters in the Republic of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Under item B of the summary, did you state that the 1990 constitution and the 1991 law of defence of the Republic of Serbia, that under those pieces of legislation, the president of the republic commanded the armed forces of the republic in peace and wartime?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, Your Honours and the underlying articles can be found in the section 3 which starts with page 60 of the English translation, or the English version, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Article 31 of the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia and that is something you're analysing on page 57, where you state that it underlines that the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia was part of the united armed forces of the SFRY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does the law on defence of the Republic of Serbia also state that only the official bodies have the authority to arm, train, and equip the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, and I would like to add that this is a particularly important part -- article, this Article 118, in light of the existence of formations that became known as paramilitary or volunteer formations which are discussed also in the second section of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is Article 31 -- does Article 31 of 1991 defence law of the Republic of Serbia provide that the Territorial Defence in the Republic of Serbia is a part of the united armed forces of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I answered that question already. It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia, as part of united armed forces of the SFRY Yugoslavia under the constitution of the SFRY and Serbia came under the federal law?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure what the word -- what the expression "came under the federal law" means, if maybe that could be explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 58 of your report, in the English version, the third paragraph is where you say that the organisation, preparation, development, and management of Territorial Defence within the united defence system is carried out according to the constitution of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, constitution of the Republic of Serbia, and the federal law. Have you understood me now?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you for the clarification. Indeed, that is mentioned in Article 31 of the 1991 defence law of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 60 of your report in the English version, you state that under Article 83, paragraph 5, of the 1990 constitution of the Republic of Serbia, that the president commanded the armed forces in peacetime and wartime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. This is paragraph 5 of Article 83 of the 1990 constitution of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the armed forces mentioned in paragraph 5 have not been defined under the constitution, and I mean the constitution of the Republic of Serbia, and that the Territorial Defence of Serbia is not mentioned either?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, based on the research I did and the documents I came across, that is a correct conclusion, which is also mentioned in this particular section of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that under Article 5 of the defence law of Serbia which you mention on page 61, the organisation of the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia shall be regulated in -- by special legislation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that's Article 5 of the 1991 defence law of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The special legislation which was to regulate the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia, was it in fact enacted, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have -- doing my research, I have not come across information that would allow to draw a conclusion or that would allow to answer that question. The reason why I included certain aspects of the legislation of the Republic of Serbia that apply to defence matters is that as you can see in section 3 of the report, on the 1st of August 1991, Milan Babic as president of the government of the SAO Krajina, with the government, adopted a decision to apply the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia on the territory known as SAO Krajina and it was only in November 1991, if I recall well, that the SAO Krajina adopted its own defence law, and this defence law is also discussed in section 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. On page 62, do you say that Articles 113 and 115 of the federal law of all people's defence from 1982 stipulated that it was the SFRY Presidency that was in command of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us on the basis of what regulation or what was the basis of your conclusion that the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia which were not defined under the law, that these were, in fact, according to you, the Territorial Defence forces?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I remember well, and I'm trying to locate the page in the report, there was mention in the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia that was adopted on the 18th of July 1991, that as long as armed forces of the republic were not defined, the TO was to serve as the armed force of the republic. Now, even without this stipulation, it was hard to imagine other armed forces for the Republic of Serbia except for the TO and under certain circumstances the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I wish to refer you to page 57, which talks about this part, where you say that the creation of the or rather that the Territorial Defence forces make up the armed forces until such forces are created.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is your answer yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I've answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how can the Territorial Defence, which is under the SFRY defence system and commanded by the SFRY Presidency, where the law on defence forces of Serbia was not enacted, where the Serbian constitution did not mention the Territorial Defence forces as the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia, how can you draw the conclusion that the TO was the armed force of Serbia in the face of all these factors which existed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, during my work here I've also been involved in interviewing witnesses for various trials and among these witnesses including also suspects for various investigations and prosecutions, there were former officials of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, and they also mentioned when discussing these articles Mr. Milovancevic has mentioned that there was an incoherence of what was mentioned in the law on defence in the Republic of Serbia on one hand and the federal legislation on the other hand. I would also like to mention that, as you have seen from my CV, I am not a legal expert. I have not spent much time on trying to find out, dining my research I have not spent much time trying to find out what the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia were at the time because that was not the purpose of my report. As I mentioned in the introduction of the report, sections 1 and sections 2 contain only that information that in my opinion was required to be able to understand section 3 and section 4. Whether the TO was the armed force of the Republic of Serbia, yes or no, in my opinion, or at the time when I drafted this report, was not an important issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Article 31 of the law on defence of the Republic of Serbia, which you mention on page 58 in the English version, at the very top, does it not explicitly stipulate that the Territorial Defence of Serbia, as part of the united armed forces of Yugoslavia, protects independence, sovereignty, territorial integrity, and constitutionally established social structure of the SFRY and Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that is correct. But all I can say is that the law of -- the law of defence here mentions Territorial Defence, whereas the constitution of the Republic of Serbia speaks about armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 64 of your report, in the section related to the duties of the Minister of Defence, do you not quote article 9 of the law on defence of Serbia from 1991 where you state that the duties of the Ministry of Defence are the civilian protection and assistance in mobilisation, and that the Ministry of Defence does not have command responsibility over the Territorial Defence or the JNA -- over the Territorial Defence in Serbia or the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, indeed that is correct. That is what the law says but I think if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours I would like to finish my reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, when you look in particular section 3 and 4, there are also examples or the evolution of the situation actually shows that the law was one thing but the application of the law was another thing, and that there may well have discrepancies at certain instances between, on one hand, what is prescribed in the law and how things should have been, and, on the other hand, how the law was applied and actually how things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you not, under item 2, mention the provisions of legislation under -- or rather of legislation in Serbia or did you in fact discuss these discrepancies?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, in section 2, not item 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as is explained in the introduction of the report, sections 1 and section 2 address legislation and regulations, i.e. how things should be -- should have been. However in section 1, I mentioned for example when addressing volunteers that notwithstanding the laws that existed and that were quite clear and we just discussed Article 118 of the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia, that didn't allow private persons or political parties to establish armed groups. In section 1, I mentioned, for example, how the legislation that applied to volunteers and was applied or not applied. So again, I didn't focus on the discrepancies in relation to the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia or the TO of the Republic of Serbia but I mentioned discrepancies where they were more relevant, the level of volunteers, the evolution of the goals of the SFRY armed forces, the evolution of the mission, I meant to say, as well as the issues discussed in section 3 and section 4 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That was not my question, Mr. Theunens. My question was: At the beginning of section 2, which is entitled, the armed forces of Serbia, do you not, under item A say that this section describes the legislative framework that applied to defence matters in the Republic of Serbia, whereas now you're discussing the practice, the [indiscernible] and something completely different? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wouldn't say it's completely different. I think there is an intimate relation between on one hand the law and on the other hand what happened. And again, yes, indeed, I understood Mr. Milovancevic asking me about certain articles of various laws and all I can answer is that indeed the quotations Mr. Milovancevic makes correspond with the text of the articles. Now, whether this also was the case in practice, that may well be another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Article 10 of the Defence law of the Republic of Serbia from 1991, which you mention on page 65 of your report, does it not say that the Minister of the Interior does not have command responsibility over the TO of the Republic of Serbia or the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that is what is written in Article 10 of the 1991 law on defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Have we not briefly now come to the conclusion that the SFRY Presidency commanded the TO defence, that the Ministry of Defence of Serbia had no command responsibility over the TO of Serbia, that the Ministry of the Interior had no command responsibility over the TO of Serbia, that the Serbian constitution does not mention the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia or the Territorial Defence and that you, in section 2, assert that the Territorial Defence constituted the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia? Is that clear, that that's in fact what you asserted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, what in all that, which one do you want the witness to answer to? In all that long paragraph, when you say, is that clear, that that's in fact what you said, what is clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Precisely. I'm referring to this last part, Your Honour, the question is rather long, but I repeated what the witness stated and my question to him, whether he stood by his position that the Territorial Defence of Serbia constituted the armed forces of Serbia, and that the section 2 he wrote was in accordance with the then valid legislation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm still not clear what you're saying. You have asked a question at paragraph 15 10 there. Have you not briefly now come to the conclusion and it goes on and then you end up by saying, "Is that clear?" Are you saying you are referring to the first part but the last part? What about the first part?.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if it will be of assistance, I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My question for the witness was: Based on the explicit provisions of the legislation we just quoted, briefly stated, that the armed forces of Serbia, under the Serbian constitution, under the SFRY constitution, under the defence law of the SFRY from 1982 and under the defence law of Serbia from 1991, that the armed forces of Serbia did not exist?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm confused by the question because do you ask me a legal question or a question on how the situation was in reality? Because if it's a legal question, then I would say, well, we looked at a number of articles and according to the law, indeed, there were -- there was no such thing as armed force of the Republic of Serbia except for the TO. However, if we look at how the law was applied and we have addressed that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Thank you, Mr. Theunens. You have answered my question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, I don't think I finished my answer, if you will allow you me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Finish your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In section 1, again without going into details, the issue of volunteers and paramilitary groups affiliated to political parties in Serbia is, based on my analysis, a good example of the situation where the law was not applied and also the issues developed in sections 3 and 4 also demonstrate that the laws and the legislation was not always applied as it had been defined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Before we go on, Mr. Milovancevic, I think you have to develop the art of breaking down your questions relating to a particular piece of legislation individually. And in all fairness to the witness, you do have to learn to distinguish between when you are stating a provision of the law as contained in his evidence as against his own conclusions that are drawn. When you proceed, I'd be grateful if you could try and do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I had in mind the conclusion that Mr. Theunens drew on page 57, item 1 b. under summary. Mr. Theunens very briefly gives a provision of the 1990 constitution and the 1991 law on defence of the Republic of Serbia, saying that the president of the republic is the commander of the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia in peace and wartime, and then he goes on to give us his own conclusion, that until the creation of such armed forces, the TO was to constitute these armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you write this, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I've answered the question extensively.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. In the introductory portion of your report, did you explain that page 1 -- or rather that the section 1 and 2 were to serve as the material enabling us to understand sections 3 and 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, it looks like you're going into a new point now. Are you going into a new point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we can have a break now. I will have several more brief questions pertaining to these issues and then we will turn to some other matters. I think this would be a good time for a break and we can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic. The Court will adjourn for 30 minutes. We'll come back at quarter to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We ended before the break at the point where we were dealing with section 2, Mr. Theunens. I have just a few more questions concerning that section. In the introductory part of your expert witness report, as well as in the introductory part on page 57 of your report, you say that the purpose of section 2 is to give the legislative framework that applied to defence matters in the Republic of Serbia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the course of your testimony, when answering the questions put to you by the Prosecution, did you state that you did not use in your work witness statements?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Am I quoting the provision of the Serbian constitution correctly when I say that the constitution of the Republic of Serbia does not define the armed forces of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to a specific article, Your Honours, or am I to answer as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to page 60, where you mention Article 83 of the constitution of Serbia, paragraph 5, wherein the chapter, president of the Serbia, item 1, you say that the armed forces are not defined in the constitution and that there is no reference in the constitution of the Territorial Defence. Is this what you wrote?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 60. What article, Mr. Milovancevic? What are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, under item 3, which is entitled "Duties of the President of the Republic of Serbia, Minister of Defence, Minister of Interior," following under A there is the president of Serbia and then a.(1) is a provision of Article 83 of the constitution of Serbia and then following that, paragraph 5 is mentioned, and then just before the quotation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's indeed what I wrote in the -- in my report on page 60, English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You speak of the legislative framework that has to do with the defence matters of the Republic of Serbia. Did you really have the legislative framework to claim what you claimed, namely that the Territorial Defence of Serbia represents the armed forces of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we are addressing this question for the third or the fourth time, but all I can say is that the constitution of the Republic of Serbia was adopted in September 1990. The articles I mention in my report speak about -- use the term armed forces without defining it. As I -- I stand by what I wrote in my report that the articles of the constitution of the Republic of Serbia of September 1990 do not mention Territorial Defence. In this section 2, I also address the law on defence of the Republic of Serbia which was adopted in July 1991, so almost a year later, and there the articles I've included in section 2 of my report, they speak about Territorial Defence and I don't think, maybe we could check it, but I don't think they mention the term armed forces. That's all I wish to answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. We have concluded with section 2. On page 66 of your expert witness report, Mr. Theunens, we have section 3 of your report, entitled, "SAO Krajina Territorial Defence. In parenthesis, 1991" is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that was a title that was provided initially -- or included initially in the report that was filed in February 2005. I would like to bring your attention to the corrigendum that was distributed at the beginning of my testimony, it has the ERN for the English version, 04668250, 04668251, and there you will see that on the second page of the corrigendum, that the title as it has been read out by Mr. Milovancevic has to be replaced with section 3, SAO Krajina/RSK TO, and then between brackets 1991-1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. It was not my intention to challenge the title as such, because in the contents portion, the title quoted there is precisely as you have just read it out to us. So I apologise to you for this misunderstanding. Under item A of the summary, you say that this section, meaning section 3, deals with the changes within the Supreme Command at the outset of the conflict in Croatia and the impact this had on the mission of the JNA during the conflict in Croatia, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Given that you have mentioned the conflict in Croatia, can you tell us who took part in the conflict and when the conflict erupted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the introduction of my report we discussed this morning, it is mentioned that my report is not a conflict analysis and doesn't, whether it comes to also the topics I have discussed doesn't intend to be a complete overview of all activities during the conflict. So to answer the question I did not study the conflict in Croatia in detail because that indeed would imply that it would also look at issues related to Croatian forces, and this answer also implies that I didn't analyse in detail when exactly the conflict in Croatia started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What you just said, Mr. Theunens, is written in the introductory part and this is something that you have already stated. What I'm interested in is whether, in drafting section 3 in its analysis, did you assess the constitutional authorities and the JNA in view of their participation in the conflict or did you perhaps use some other method?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I did is I compared the constitutional mission as it had been defined in the 1974 constitution and confirmed in the 1982 all people's defence law, and then I looked at a number of sources that actually describes the role of the JNA during the conflict in Croatia. The sources I used are mentioned in the beginning of section 3. They include the book by develop Veljko Kadijevic, My View of the Break-up. I also looked at the book by Borisav Jovic who was the outgoing president of the SFRY Presidency in May 1991 but who stayed in the Presidency, his book is called, "Last days of the SFRY." And then I also looked at contemporaneous JNA documents or statements of the SFRY Supreme Command staff, in order to come to a description of what the JNA actually did during the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you state in item B, when talking about the constitutional mission of the SFRY armed forces, that starting in the summer of 1991, following the JNA's withdrawal from Slovenia, the situation in Croatia evolved in such a way that the role of the armed forces became less clear from a military point of view?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: When giving such a conclusion, did you take into account the development of the situation and events in Croatia? I'm referring to this period of time that you're analysing.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, the sources I mentioned in my reply to the previous question obviously discuss the situation in -- the development of the situation in Croatia, because it's an inherent part in the change of mission of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does this answer mean that you did take into account the development of the situation in Croatia during the conflict in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I should be more clear. What I did was I took into account or I used the information contained in the sources I mentioned to -- not only to draft the section but also to understand how again these sources saw the evolution of the situation in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that the acts of the SFRY armed forces in Croatia in 1991, in the summer of 1991, following the withdrawal of the JNA from Slovenia, at the time when there was a conflict in Croatia, was something that you took into account as acts of one armed forces without taking into account the acts of the other side to the conflict, and that you have no information about the acts of the other side?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's an incorrect representation of the answer I gave to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 68 of your report, under the heading, "The SFRY armed forces at the outset of the conflict in Croatia," or on the eve of the conflict of Croatia, under item A you discuss the overall command and control; is that correct, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, the chart represents the structure as it existed in peacetime. Of course, once one of the three states is being declared, a state of emergency, a state of imminent threat of war or a state of war, then as I have explained in the first section of the report, certain changes would occur whereby, for example, the federal Presidency would become the Supreme Command and the federal Secretariat for national -- for people's defence, together with the General Staff would become the staff of the Supreme Command, whereby the federal secretary for people's defence, in this situation army general Kadijevic would become the Chief of Staff of the staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On the same page, page 68 of your report, do you state that on the 15th of May 1991, Stipe Mesic, the Croatian member of the SFRY Presidency, who was supposed to take over the role of the president of the Presidency, failed to obtain the necessary quorum from the other members of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I would like to add that I also mention in the footnote 201 the views Borisav Jovic, who was the outgoing chairman of the SFRY Presidency, the views Borisav Jovic had on the circumstances of the failure of Mesic to obtain the necessary quorum.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The issue of the election of the president of Presidency, is it something that is regulated by the rules of procedure of that body, the Presidency? Did you hear of such a document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm now referring to the Presidency of the SFRY, which was a collective body. I simply wanted to ask the witness whether he knew that the work and the functioning of the Presidency of such a collective body was regulated by an enactment, a type of a document that regulated rules of procedure, how the votes were to be taken and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does the witness know about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, on -- in section 1, so on page 13 of the English version, I only list a number of articles of the 1974 SFRY constitution that deal with the Presidency. I didn't analyse the rules of procedure or other aspects related to the Presidency in detail, because I believed that it was outside of the tasking I received when starting to compile this report or to draft this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were aware of the fact that in order to elect a president of the Presidency, a quorum is needed as well as a majority of votes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, again I didn't analyse the rules of procedure, and I think that in the context of the issues we are discussing, the information mentioned in footnote 201, so at the bottom of page 68 of the English version, is more relevant. According to what Borisav Jovic, who was - again I mentioned it earlier - the outgoing chairman of the Presidency, and he was also a representative of the Republic of Serbia in the SFRY Presidency, Jovic wrote in his published diary, and that's entry for 13th of May, that he, Slobodan Milosevic, who was the president of Serbia, Momir Bulatovic, who was the president of Montenegro, and Jugoslav Kostic had agreed that Mesic could not be elected. I considered this entry more important when discussing the evolution of the mission of the JNA than rules of procedure which would have been addressed in section 1, i.e. the de jure situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it clear then, that following the voting process in the SFRY, the voting of the attending members, Mr. Mesic did not have the necessary number of votes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I don't want to interfere with your line of cross-examination, but I thought that you put to the witness a little earlier that Mr. Mesic couldn't even get a quorum. Am I right? Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just put to the expert witness, Mr. Theunens, the text on page 68, under the chart, federal Presidency of the SFRY. The paragraph underneath it, beginning with the words, "On 15th of May," continues on to say that Mr. Mesic was not elected president of the Presidency because, as the witness says, he failed to obtain the necessary quorum. What I'm trying to clarify is that Mr. Mesic failed to obtain the necessary number of votes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, I'm asking you my question once again: Am I right to say that that paragraph you've just quoted says Mr. Mesic didn't get a quorum?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if he didn't get a quorum, how can there be a vote? There is no meeting. If there is no meeting the meeting can't take place. Isn't that so? So the voting cannot take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I'd like it say this. The witness just explained to us, by referring to footnote 201, that he quoted the words of Borisav Jovic who, until then, was president of the Presidency and was a Serbian member of the Presidency. He said that four members of the Presidency voted against appointment of Mr. Mesic and then I followed up on the explanation that the witness gave to my question. I am not here to draw your attention to the fact that the witness is legally unqualified to distinguish between a majority of votes and a quorum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, where in that footnote does the witness say that that they couldn't get a vote, that the Presidency voted against him? Where does he say that? Because all I see here is that he says that they agreed that he could not be elected. I don't see where he says that they voted against him or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the interpretation of what Mr. Milovancevic said?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in putting these questions, I only intend to get the witness's answer. That's to say whether the SFRY Presidency elected Stjepan Mesic when his voting was to be processed or not, and the witness answered that there was no quorum. However, to me, the important issue is whether the SFRY Presidency elected Mr. Mesic when the time came for his election to take place or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Milovancevic, if that's what you want to do, then do it. Don't do what you have been doing. Because what you have been doing is you are asking him questions which don't follow from the document before us, number 1. Number 2, which don't follow ordinary logic. Logic says if there is no quorum, there can be no meeting, therefore there can be no voting. What's before us says that -- on the footnote there, that the other people there agreed that Mesic shall not be elected, could not be elected. There is no where where it says that they voted against him. So put questions to the witness that are correct and not misleading, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It was not my intention to put questions to the witness that would mislead him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That was the effect, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry and I will do my best not to have this happen again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On this same page, did you not write that after the intervention of the European Union, Mr. Mesic was elected president of the Presidency of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I wrote is that Mr. Mesic assumed the position or the post of president of the Presidency. Now, it was not part of my report to analyse the circumstances of the election or the appointment of Mr. Mesic to the position of president of the SFRY Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, my question was as follows: You said that after the intervention of the European Union, Mr. Mesic assumed the post of president of the Presidency of Yugoslavia. Now, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I answered that question. It's implied in the answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not implied it's absolutely correct, that's what he said there: "Mr. Mesic assumed the post of the president of the Presidency."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 69, do you state this is at the top of the page under item 2, that the federal secretary for people's defence, General Veljko Kadijevic, did not recognise Mesic as the new Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is a conclusion based on what Kadijevic not only wrote in his book in 1993, My View of the Break-up, but also when we review the exhibit -- and I'm identifying the document -- the document with 65 ter number 1850, also shows Kadijevic's views or his attitude towards Mr. Mesic as Supreme Commander. Exhibit 65 ter 1850 is discussed on page 77 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Below paragraph 2, when explaining why the secretary for people's defence did not recognise Mesic as the new Supreme Commander, do you not give a quotation which says there were two reasons for this, Mesic could not have any personal influence as president of the Presidency because among other things he had already publicly compromised [as interpreted] himself as the destroyer of Yugoslavia, and because of his attempts to gain influence looked ridiculous, and that there were orders he issued through the media and which the Supreme Command simply ignored?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I think it's very serious when the Supreme Command symbolised by General Kadijevic does not recognise his Supreme Commander. That is clearly visible through the quotation you mentioned, the quotation from Kadijevic's book in which Kadijevic expresses his views on Mesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Mr. Kadijevic in his book, which is Exhibit 1370, explicitly states on page 35, in the B/C/S, you say that you read the book, you should remember, that he says that at the end of 1989, the events in Yugoslavia were practically in the hands of an international players; is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did read General Kadijevic's book several times but I don't recall what his exactly what is mentioned on page 35. So if I'm to comment on page 35 I would like to have it in front of me. And otherwise I can only say, well, that the book reflects Kadijevic's views.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Having read the book, do you remember, I only mentioned one sentence from page 35, rather than quoting the entire page, that on page 37, Kadijevic says that the attitude of the international community towards the JNA had several stages, the first one was to have Stjepan Mesic assume the position of president of SFRY Presidency with a view to having control over the army? Do you recall such an assertion by General Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I'm expected to comment on it, I would prefer to have the English page in front of me. That would make it easier for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Without the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Without the book before you, do you recall or don't you recall that kind of fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, from the book, one can conclude indeed that not only Kadijevic but a number of people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, Mr. -- do you understand my question? My question to you is without the book before you, are you able to recall that statement that had been made to you and your answer is then I can recall or I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact statement. I know the general flavour of it, Your Honour, but I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, and this has to do with the part of the text you quoted, which we heard a moment ago, which were the reasons why General Kadijevic did not recognise Mesic, that in his book on the same page that you quoted here, Mr. Kadijevic says, and this is under the same chapter, that this initial attempt by the representatives of the international community --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, of the European Community.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: To have Mr. Mesic assume the position of SFRY Presidency with a view to assuming control over the army, drew to a close quite soon because they realised that they could not have any control over the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I apologise for the interruption. This shouldn't really be a memory test. He's asked now twice to see the document. It's Exhibit 24 in evidence. I think the witness ought to be allowed to see it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to put questions this way, Your Honour, because I thought that this would allow me to go through the topics in a more rapid manner. If the witness were familiar with this, especially with the matters on page 37. The reason why I'm putting these questions is that the sense of what I'm quoting right now was distorted and that's why I'm showing this to the witness without presenting the book to him. If you agree with me that we should present the witness with the document, then we could take it page by page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I follow your argument but you understand that this is not a memory test for the witness. I'm not sure whether -- are you questioning his memory on issues or are you questioning his -- the conclusions he drew given the information that he had before him? I'm not quite sure what you are doing, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps the Registry should, and this has to do with the 65 ter Exhibit number 1370, perhaps the Registry could show us page 37. This is Exhibit 24 admitted in this case through the first witness. The reason I'm suggesting this is that, on page 69, the witness quoted one part of Mr. Kadijevic's words in such a way that the sense of what was said has been completely changed, and this can be in fact seen only once we look at this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which is why, then, you must allow that he be given the page, sir. Can he be given the document, then? Then you can confront him with the incorrect quotations. Then in which event then I should -- I will -- the objection will be upheld. Provide the witness with the book, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this exhibit has been admitted, Exhibit 1370 has been already admitted as Prosecution Exhibit 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Get it pulled out, Mr. Milovancevic. Let's see it on the ELMO or wherever we can see it or in hard copy, and let the witness get a copy of it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 24, and could we look at page 37 in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would imagine that the Bench will require the English version also.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's any assistance, I have not identified the specific page in the English he's talking about but I think it should start after 00362703, that being the ERN of the first page that discusses the war in Croatia. If that gets us closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have page 71 on the screen in the B/C/S, whereas we need to find page 37, and then the corresponding English page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please get page 37 in the B/C/S on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is a request for the ERN number of the particular page to be able to get to page 37, please. Can you give us that, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please, Your Honour. [Defence counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that's 0035-9445; in the B/C/S, it should be page 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.
